text:
Frederic Brunet was a fifth-round pick in 2022, a long shot from Gatineau who had played one NHL game before this season. Now he's a regular on Boston's blue line at about 16 minutes a night, with a goal and 5 points in 14 games, two of them on the power play.

That's the good part, and it's worth something for a 23-year-old who was 132nd overall. The harder part is the five on five play. With Brunet on the ice the Bruins have taken about 44% of shot attempts and expected goals, almost 12 points worse than without him. Only 38% of his even-strength time comes in the offensive zone, which is a rookie's tough introduction in one number.

Boston has lost three straight, with 5-2 and 6-2 defeats to Montreal and Minnesota in two of the games Brunet played. He's young and getting real minutes. Whether the Bruins keep giving them to him while the shot share sits where it does is what we'd watch.
